name: Valençay

limits: For white wine, Sauvignon Blanc: at least 70%
For red wine, Pinot Noir: at least 10%
For red wine, Malbec: at least 10%
For red wine, Cabernet Franc: at most 20%
For rosé wine, Pinot Noir: at least 10%
For rosé wine, Malbec: at least 10%
For rosé wine, Cabernet Franc: at most 20%
For rosé wine, Pineau d'Aunis: at most 30%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for white, 55 for red and rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

blurb.text: A Touraine appellation in the upper Loire, on the left bank of the Cher. The name is shared with a protected goat's cheese. Sauvignon Blanc is the main white grape, and reds are made from Malbec, Gamay and Pinot Noir.
